scope: Theorem 8.2 (Sufficiently general finite subgroups) of the manuscript “Finite congruence lattices: characterization and undecidability” (preprints/Finite-Congruence-Lattices-Characterization-and-Undecidability-September-24-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 206 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 d26d6cd6285de4f2), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 53. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: For the fixed finite list of simple adjoint types, there is a uniform degree bound d0 with the following property. If a finite subgroup Γ ≤ G(k), where k = Fp, is contained in no proper closed subset of equation complexity at most d0, then there is a Steinberg map Ψ such that (GΨ )′ ≤ Γ ≤ GΨ . Here the degree bound follows from the uniform constructible-family formulation of the sufficiently- general subgroup theorem of Larsen–Pink [25, Theorem 0.5 and Metadefinition 2.2]: the exceptional family has uniformly bounded defining equations in the fixed affine models.
